Study data and downloads

study-data.Rmd

Study background and citation

The demonstration uses publicly available pancreatic tumor microbiome data from Riquelme and colleagues, Tumor Microbiome Diversity and Composition Influence Pancreatic Cancer Outcomes, Cell (2019), DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2019.07.008. Please cite the original paper when using these data. The downloads below provide processed PICRUSt2 inputs for testing MicroFun. For additional study information, contact Dr. Liangliang Zhang at lxz716@case.edu.

The dataset contains 68 samples and 2,487 ASVs after excluding 290 ASVs assigned to Genus Incertae sedis. The MDA discovery cohort has 43 samples, with 22 STS and 21 LTS. The JHU validation cohort has 25 samples, with 10 STS and 15 LTS. The demonstration code defaults to MDA, matching the 43-sample Standard figure exports. Change the cohort explicitly to analyze JHU separately.

Table 1. Cohorts in the processed demonstration data
Cohort Role STS LTS Total
MDA Discovery 22 21 43
JHU Validation 10 15 25
All supplied samples Both cohorts 32 36 68

Sample identifiers have been replaced consistently with S001 to S068. Metadata retain only the new sample identifier, survival group, cohort and cohort role. Original sample aliases and sequencing run identifiers are omitted. The same replacement is used in the abundance tables, contribution tables, OTU table and phyloseq object.

Why Genus Incertae sedis was removed

Incertae sedis denotes uncertain taxonomic placement rather than a resolved genus. Combining ASVs under that placeholder would treat potentially distinct lineages as a single biological contributor. We removed the 290 ASVs carrying this Genus label so the genus-level comparison focuses on interpretable, assigned genera. This is a taxonomic scope decision, not evidence of contamination or absence of biological function. See the NCBI Taxonomy description of uncertain placement.

The filter was applied consistently to the phyloseq object, taxonomy, OTU table, tree and all contribution tables. Standard profiles were regenerated from the filtered contributions. The core archive includes filter_summary.csv and removed_ASVs.csv to document the excluded ASVs. Sample groups and sample identifiers are unchanged.

Choose the files for your analysis

Complete installation and dependencies in a fresh R session before running the code below.

Start with the core archive for the Standard demonstration. For the Stratified demonstration, also download both KO contribution parts. The taxon-centered route aggregates KOs into pathways; the function-centered example selects 23 project-related KOs from the same file. The dated KEGG, EC and MetaCyc contributions are available for alternative workflows.

Table 2. Downloadable demonstration inputs
Download Approximate size Contents
Core data 2.2 MiB All Standard profiles, deidentified metadata, phyloseq/R data, OTU table, taxonomy, ASV tree and assembly script.
KEGG Stratified contributions 14.7 MiB An alternative preaggregated KEGG pathway snapshot.
KO Stratified part 1 80.0 MiB First transfer part of the KO contribution table. Both parts are required.
KO Stratified part 2 32.3 MiB Second transfer part of the same KO contribution table.
EC Stratified contributions 55.0 MiB EC contribution table.
MetaCyc Stratified contributions 42.2 MiB MetaCyc contribution table.

Use one R project folder for all three pages and keep its working directory unchanged. Run getwd() to see where R expects the ZIP files. Download files with the filenames shown below and leave them zipped until running the extraction code.

Use these updated archives together in a fresh project folder. Do not combine them with an earlier demonstration-data release. Each ZIP contains a folder named MicroFun_demonstration_data_filtered. Save your chosen archives in the R working directory, then extract them into the same location. The two KO parts are transfer fragments, not separate input tables. The included script reconstructs one complete gzip file and verifies its checksum.

# Install the software first using the installation guide.
# Use the fixed vegan release in a fresh R session.
stopifnot(requireNamespace("vegan", quietly = TRUE),
          getNamespaceVersion("vegan") == package_version("2.7.2"))

# Core data for both demonstrations.
stopifnot(file.exists("MicroFun_filtered_core.zip"))
unzip("MicroFun_filtered_core.zip", exdir = ".")

data_dir <- normalizePath("MicroFun_demonstration_data_filtered", mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(data_dir, "assemble-data.R"), local = new.env(), chdir = TRUE)

For either stratified analysis, download both KO parts and run these additional lines.

ko_archives <- c("MicroFun_filtered_KO_part01.zip",
                 "MicroFun_filtered_KO_part02.zip")
stopifnot(all(file.exists(ko_archives)))
unzip("MicroFun_filtered_KO_part01.zip", exdir = ".")
unzip("MicroFun_filtered_KO_part02.zip", exdir = ".")
source(file.path(data_dir, "assemble-data.R"), local = new.env(), chdir = TRUE)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(data_dir, "stratified", "KO_contrib.tsv.gz")))

Files after extraction

Table 3. Paths used by the demonstrations
Relative path inside MicroFun_demonstration_data_filtered Description
phyloseq_asv.RData Objects named ps, metadata, otu, taxonomy and phylo_tree.
metadata.tsv New sample identifiers, group, Cohort and CohortRole.
otu.tsv.gz, taxonomy.tsv, asv_tree.nwk ASV-level abundance, taxonomy and phylogeny.
standard/KO.tsv.gz 8,881 KO features across all 68 samples.
standard/KEGG_2026-11-04.tsv.gz 234 KEGG pathways across all 68 samples.
standard/EC.tsv.gz, standard/MetaCyc.tsv.gz 2,898 EC features and 542 MetaCyc pathways.
stratified/KEGG_2026-11-04_contrib.tsv.gz Alternative dated pathway input, used with pathway = "KEGG".
stratified/KO_contrib.tsv.gz Reconstructed KO table for taxon-centered and function-centered analyses.
standard/KO_figure_features.csv, standard/KEGG_figure_features.csv Feature selections used in the supplied figure exports.
manifest.csv Included file sizes and MD5 checksums.
filter_summary.csv, removed_ASVs.csv Taxonomic filtering summary and removed ASV identifiers.
KO_display_labels.csv Optional author-supplied KO display names for Chord presentation. KO IDs remain the analysis keys.

The KEGG filenames preserve the date of the supplied pathway-table export. The underlying KO-to-pathway membership file is not included in this download. To keep the displayed examples consistent, the Standard and taxon-centered demonstrations aggregate KOs with the bundled mapping. The dated 234-pathway snapshot has different coverage; it does not reproduce the displayed KEGG PCA. With the bundled mapping and MDA samples, the first two KEGG PCA axes explain 56.0% and 14.3%. See mapping and annotation before choosing another mapping.

Load and select a cohort 

library(phyloseq)
study <- new.env()
load(file.path(data_dir, "phyloseq_asv.RData"), envir = study)
ps <- study$ps
cohort <- "MDA"
ps <- prune_samples(sample_data(ps)$Cohort == cohort, ps)
ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)
meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))
table(meta$group)

Standard profiles and contribution files retain all 68 samples so that either cohort can be selected. Both demonstrations use the chosen sample identifiers to subset the corresponding inputs.

Continue with Demonstration Study (Standard), then Demonstration Study (Stratified), using the same R project folder.

The Stratified demonstration uses Genus-level aggregation. Its taxon-centered route selects 27 project-related genera, while its function-centered route selects 23 project-related KOs and retains all genus contributors in the filtered data. Standard remains a community-level analysis. The source taxonomy supports Phylum through Genus; its Species column is entirely unassigned.
